I’d pitch three or four new show ideas in a day, start rewriting old scripts at 2 a.m., rearrange my entire apartment between drafts. I was sleeping maybe three hours a night, but I’d wake up buzzing, not tired at all. My thoughts were nonstop, like they were overlapping—jumping from scene ideas to podcast concepts to texting people—and I couldn’t slow them down long enough to really focus on one thing. I’d start a script, check emails, open Twitter, then another draft, all in minutes.

Then it crashed. For the last two months, I can’t feel anything good. Even when an episode does well, it’s flat. I’m exhausted just walking to the subway; my body feels like it weighs a ton. I keep replaying stupid things I’ve said in writers’ meetings from years ago and just hating myself for them. I do feel anxious—like a constant hum in the background—but those earlier racing thoughts and impulsive bursts weren’t really about worry; they just sort of took over on their own. Now both phases have messed up my work—I’ve missed deadlines, blown up at people, and lately I can barely write at all.
